newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hillary Clinton awed by ancient Mayan site.
newsitem.headline: Hillary Clinton awed by ancient Mayan site.

text.p: U.S. First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton on Monday visited the massive Uxmal pyramid, one of the master works of Mayan architecture, saying she was overwhelmed by the sight but choosing not to climb to its 125 foot (38 metre) summit.

A keen hiker, the wife of U.S. President Bill Clinton had wanted to climb the 1,000-year-old pyramid, which rises dramatically out of dense forest in the Yucatan peninsula, but found its crumbling limestone too rugged for her shoes.
"We think of ourselves as troopers ... but I wore the wrong shoes," she said as others scaled the building. "I am going to watch in wonder, amazement, jealousy, envy."
Mrs. Clinton had hoped to tour the complex with her husband, who begins a visit to Mexico on Monday evening.

But Clinton tore a tendon in his knee in mid-March, putting him on crutches and leaving Hillary to take in the Pyramid of the Magician and the rest of the Uxmal complex, believed to have been built by the Mayans between 700 and 1,000 A.D., by herself.

"I am overwhelmed at the size of it and at the complexity of the carvings and the iconography that we see here," Mrs. Clinton said as she surveyed the group of buildings from the elaborately carved Palace of the Governor.
Mrs. Clinton began her trip to Mexico a day before her husband, flying to Merida, the capital of Yucatan state, on Sunday evening.

On Monday morning she drove 50 miles (80.5 km) south to Uxmal to take in the Mayan complex, which is dominated by the elliptically shaped pyramid. Archaelogists believe the complex was a site for religious devotion, including human sacrifice, and served as a residence and seat of government for elites.
Mayan civilisation in the Uxmal region collapsed before the early 16th century Spanish conquest of Mexico, with drought and overpopulation among the causes speculated for its demise.

Mrs. Clinton was scheduled to meet a group of local women before flying to Mexico City evening to join her husband for the May 5-7 visit, and then travel to Costa Rica and Barbados for regional summit meetings.

Despite his knee injury, Clinton is scheduled to visit a pyramid complex at Teotihuacan near Mexico City but will do so without climbing. "He will be able to view the buildings ... without having to get out and walk," Mrs. Clinton said.
